_note: v8 cut (<=45 s). Hook = the real report with 'sold above range' on the rabbit night light. One shop (fictional online gift shop), one dataset (public UK gift-shop export, replayed as of 27 Nov 2011), plain English headers ('Pieces' and 'Day Sold' are the two the header rules cannot place). All numbers come from the recorded run (demo/raw-v8, runs/20261017-221903-dc1811) and eval/results.

scenes.src: row: Rabbit night light-1.0..row: Rabbit night light+3.5
scenes.caption: Week of 28 Nov 2011. Rabbit night light: expected 1,249, really sold 4,452
scenes.text: The forecast said twelve hundred rabbit night lights. The shop sold forty-four hundred.

scenes.caption: Real app. Public UK gift-shop export, date typed: replay as of 27 Nov 2011, labelled demo data
scenes.text: It starts here. A made-up shop owner drops in her order export. The data is a public UK file, replayed.

scenes.caption: Headers the rules cannot place (Pieces, Day Sold) go to Gemma, on this laptop
scenes.text: Two headers the rules can't place. Gemma, running on the laptop, reads them.

scenes.caption: Real run: 138 s on a laptop CPU, log sped up. TabPFN-2 forecasts, Gemma writes
scenes.text: Code cleans a million rows. Tab P F N forecasts twenty regular sellers, with a range for each. Gemma writes the note.

scenes.caption: The restock note. Code checks every number in it
scenes.text: Out comes a restock note, with each product's chance of selling out. Code checks every number.

scenes.src: row: Red harmonica-0.3..row: Rabbit night light+2.0
scenes.caption: 17 of 20 inside their range. Rabbit night light sold above it (its sell-out chance said 7 percent)
scenes.text: Seventeen of twenty sold inside their range. The rabbit night light did not, and its sell-out chance said seven percent. The post shows this miss.
